content.title: About
content.content: Swordfish (Xiphias gladius) is a large pelagic fish found in open oceans. Wild‑caught and flash‑frozen, it retains its natural flavor, firm texture, and high nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Swordfish can grow over 4.5 m in length and weigh more than 600 kg.
Its distinctive elongated bill is used for hunting and defense.
Unlike many fish, swordfish has no scales; its skin is smooth and covered with a thin mucus layer.
It is considered a delicacy in Japan, often served as sashimi.
In the US and Europe the wild population is regarded as sustainable, though some regions impose catch limits.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Swordfish provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other fish, swordfish is low in saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Contains EPA and DHA, which promote heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: High in B12, niacin, and B6, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting antioxidant defenses and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: As a large predatory fish, swordfish can accumulate mercury; pregnant women and young children should limit intake.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: People allergic to fish may react to swordfish.

items.title: Sodium in processing
items.content: Frozen products may be brined; check labels if you need low‑sodium options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Swordfish can be baked, grilled, steamed, or used in sushi and sashimi. Thaw in the refrigerator, pat dry, then season with lemon, olive oil, herbs, or soy sauce before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen swordfish at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Discard any fish with off‑odors or discoloration.
